They have also been instructed to take necessary steps to bring Sudarshan Goud’s mortal remains back to the country.

stories.headline: Delhi High Court Directs Authorities To Provide Industrialist Anil Ambani's Son Details Of LOC Against Him
stories.title: Delhi High Court Directs Authorities To Provide Industrialist Anil Ambani's Son Details Of LOC Against Him
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Delhi High Court has directed the authorities to provide Jai Anshul Anil Ambani, son of industrialist Anil Ambani, specific details of the Look Out Circular (LOC) issued against him, including the date of its issuance, and a copy of the formal order.
Justice Mini Pushkarna passed the direction while hearing an application filed by Jai Anshul seeking compliance of an earlier order passed on September 17 by a coordinate bench.

The Court was informed that the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) had communicated to Jai Anshul on October 05 that an LOC had been issued against him in view of an ongoing investigation and that it continued to remain in force.
However, his counsel submitted that the communication was vague and did not disclose specific details regarding the LOC.
Taking note of the communication, the Court directed the authorities to provide details regarding when the LOC was issued and furnish a copy of the formal order to Jai Anshul in accordance with law.
The Court also took note of Ambani's submission that the communication was received only from the SFIO and not from the Bureau of Immigration.

“Accordingly, respondents are further directed to apprise the Court as to whether any other LOC has been issued against the petitioner, which is in the knowledge of the Bureau of Immigration,” the Court said.

During the hearing, counsel for the authorities submitted that the earlier direction had required the petition to be treated as a representation and requisite intimation to be provided within a time-bound manner.
It was argued that the Court had not directed the authorities to furnish specific details of the LOC.
The respondents also submitted that if Jai Anshul was dissatisfied with the communication issued by the SFIO, he could pursue other remedies available to him.
The matter will be considered next on October 16.

stories.headline: Karnataka High Court Directs Police To Secure LOC Against Husband In Dowry Case
stories.title: Karnataka High Court Directs Police To Secure LOC Against Husband In Dowry Case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Karnataka High Court on Monday [October 12] directed the police to take steps for the issuance of the Look Out Circular (LOC) against the husband of a woman who has accused him of cruelty and dowry harassment, while ordering hand delivery of the order.

The single judge bench of Justice Anant Ramananth Hegde passed the interim direction while hearing a criminal petition filed by the wife seeking a direction to the police to issue LOC against her husband- a working professional at France.
The direction is subject to Court's final order.

The wife has contended that her husband remains in India only for the reissuance of his supposedly lost passport, and that his departure afterwards would irretrievably damage her cause and further investigation in the FIR.
The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) had in October rejected her application under Section 175(3) r/w Section 94 of the BNSS for the same reliefs.

Yesterday, when the matter was taken up, Advocate Angad Kamath, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that not intimating the respondent husband about the issuance of the LOC would not infringe upon his rights under the Constitution of India, and that the LOC can be issued subject to the guidelines issued therein.

“…It is well settled that mere inability to pay the money without there being a criminal case cannot be a reason to take away the fundamental right guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India…”.

Kamath submitted that while dowry harassment is part of the allegations, the purported inability to pay money by the accused, as mentioned by the magistrate in the order, had nothing to do with the case or the issuance of the LOC sought for.
He pointed out that there are two named accused, the mother-in-law and the husband.
The husband is a resident of France, and once he goes back, he cannot be secured for investigation.
Though he is a passport holder of India, he has been a resident of France for 3 years, Kamath added.
He holds a visa of Tunisia and France, and all he requires is a boarding pass to leave the country forever, it was submitted further.

stories.title: Congress stages protest in Hubballi seeking resignation of Chief Election Commissioner
stories.summary: Congress workers staged a protest rally in Hubballi on October 12, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral malpractice and attempts to undermine democracy
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Congress workers staged a protest rally in Hubballi on October 11, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral malpractice and attempts to undermine democracy.

The rally was organised by the Vidyanagar and Unkal block Congress committees under the leadership of Rajat Ullagaddimath, Chairperson of the Hubballi-Dharwad City District Guarantee Schemes Implementation Authority.
It began at Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Circle, where the protesters read out Article 326 of the Constitution, which provides for elections based on adult suffrage.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Ullagaddimath alleged that the RSS is conspiring to deprive oppressed and marginalised communities of their right to vote.
Describing the struggle to protect democracy and the Constitution as a ‘second freedom struggle’ against what he termed fascist forces, he called for concerted action to safeguard electoral rights.

Hundreds of Congress workers accused the BJP-led Union Government of attempting to manipulate the votes of Other Backward Classes, Economically Weaker Sections, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and minority communities.
They raised slogans against the Centre and demanded Mr. Kumar’s resignation.
Tension prevailed when the rally reached the Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation office.
Protesters allegedly attempted to burn portraits of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and Mr. Kumar, triggering a scuffle between the police and the demonstrators.
The police, subsequently, detained several protesters.

Hubballi-Dharwad District Congress president Sadanand Danganavar, I.G. Sanadi, KPCC member Satish Meharwade, Shahzaman Mujahid, Anwar Mudgol, Mohammed Sharif Gargad, and several councillors and party functionaries participated in the protest.

stories.headline: Kerala Congress Faces BJP Attack Over SIR After UDF’s Election Victory
stories.title: Kerala Congress Faces BJP Attack Over SIR After UDF’s Election Victory
stories.summary: Kerala’s Congress-led UDF government faces BJP criticism after the state Assembly passed a resolution seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal and questioning the voter-roll revision exercise that preceded its election victory.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Kerala’s Congress-led UDF government faces BJP criticism after the state Assembly passed a resolution seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal and questioning the voter-roll revision exercise that preceded its election victory.

The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Kerala has come under fire from the BJP after the state Assembly passed a resolution questioning the Election Commission of India’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The resolution has sparked a political controversy because the UDF swept to power in the Assembly elections in May, months after the voter-roll revision was completed.
The BJP has accused the Congress of contradicting itself by challenging the credibility of an electoral process that preceded its victory.
The controversy has also drawn attention to remarks by senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor, who had suggested that the SIR exercise might have benefited the party in Kerala.
On Monday, the Kerala Assembly passed the resolution with 137 of its 140 members voting in its favour.
The three BJP MLAs opposed the bill, which is said to be the first of its kind in the nation.

The resolution demands the removal of Chief Minister VD Satheesan, restoration of names of eligible voters whose names were deleted in the SIR exercise and changes in the appointment process of the election commissioners, the Chief Minister said.

Satheesan however said that the matter needed to be discussed as there were some concerns about the roll revision procedure, the potential exclusion of eligible citizens and the neutrality of the Election Commission.
In a post on X, he said the integrity of the electoral process was non-negotiable and described the right to vote as a foundation of democracy.
The resolution aligns with the Congress’s broader national campaign against the SIR process and its demand for action against the Chief Election Commissioner.
Kerala was included in the second phase of the nationwide SIR exercise announced on October 27, 2025, alongside Assam, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry.

stories.headline: Can CEC and Election Commissioners be prosecuted? Supreme Court examines legal immunity
stories.title: Can CEC and Election Commissioners be prosecuted? Supreme Court examines legal immunity
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court will examine a challenge to the legal immunity granted to the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners under the 2023 law.
The case raises questions about whether the protection of election officials from civil and criminal proceedings is consistent with constitutional accountability.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court has issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India (ECI) on a petition filed by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) challenging the legal immunity granted to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners for acts performed in the discharge of their official duties.

The challenge targets Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which bars courts from entertaining or continuing civil or criminal proceedings against serving or former election commissioners for acts or statements made in the discharge, or purported discharge, of their official functions.
The petition has been tagged with related matters pending before the court and is scheduled to be heard alongside them on October 29.
The Supreme Court's latest notice brings the statutory protection available to India's top election officials under judicial scrutiny.

The petition, filed by ADR, challenges Section 16 of the 2023 Act, which provides immunity from civil and criminal proceedings for acts, things or words committed, done or spoken by a serving or former Chief Election Commissioner or Election Commissioner in the discharge, or purported discharge, of official duties.
The court has sought responses from the Union government and the Election Commission.
Issuing notice means the respondents have been asked to present their position; it does not mean the court has held the provision unconstitutional.

The case raises a fundamental legal question: how far can Parliament protect election commissioners from litigation arising out of their official functions without undermining the constitutional principles of accountability and the rule of law?
The provision does not, by its wording, extend to every act an election commissioner might commit in a personal capacity.
Its stated scope concerns conduct connected with the discharge, or purported discharge, of official duties.

stories.headline: Saudis probe how defence systems failed to stop deadly Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
stories.title: Saudis probe how defence systems failed to stop deadly Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
stories.summary: Cairo, Oct 13: Saudi Arabia has launched an investigation to determine how its air defences failed to intercept a barrage of missiles and drones fired by Iran-backed Houthi rebels, including an attack on Riyadh airport that killed at least 13 people and wounded over 300, two regional officials said Monday. The officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly, said the initial probe showed that Yemen's Houthis first fired multiple drones to pave the way for a mix of cruise and ballistic missiles to reach Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. The Houthis possess ballistic missiles and advanced systems fitted with warheads that can change direction during flight and pose a challenge to Patriot interceptors and other defence systems used by the Saudis. One of the officials said the investigation also aims to find out why air defence systems did not provide earlier warning of the attack in which the Houthi missiles and drones flew over 1,000 kilometres (620 miles) to reach Riyadh. The incident, one of a string of Houthi attacks since last week on Saudi airports, has exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi Arabia's defence system and signalled a dangerous inflexion point in an expanding Middle East conflict that began more than seven months ago when the US and Israel launched their war against Iran. The Saudi-led coalition also said it had twice intercepted and destroyed ballistic missiles launched Monday by Yemen's Houthi rebels toward Riyadh. At least three explosions could be heard Monday night in the city. There was no immediate claim of responsibility. Civil Defence officials later said the danger had passed. Earlier on Monday, the Saudi state-run media reported that its military was responding to a new attack involving drones and cruise missiles, but provided no details. “The events of recent weeks are serious," Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman told the World Petroleum Energy Congress in Riyadh on Monday. “Our response must be equally serious.” The Saudi government-run Centre for International Communication, which oversees foreign media, did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the probe into defence failures. Saudi officials want more US help in countering Houthi attacks The Saudis want the US to become more directly involved in their fight against the Houthis. The US has provided intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for a Saudi-led offensive, but has held off on carrying out strikes against the Houthis. A US intervention could prompt the Houthis to try to halt shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea off Yemen, restricting the flow of oil out of the Persian Gulf. The flow of Middle East oil has already been complicated by Iranian efforts to choke off the Strait of Hormuz, where about one-fifth of the world's oil flowed before the US-Iran war began. The rebels seized key areas along the Bab el-Mandeb last month. The Saudi-led coalition, backing forces aligned with Yemen's internationally recognised government, has been trying to retake them. US President Donald Trump told reporters on Saturday after the deadly airport strike that he was looking at the possibility of carrying out US attacks against the Houthis. But the conflict comes at a delicate time for Trump, just weeks before US midterm elections that will decide if his Republican Party keeps control of Congress. Persistent inflation and high gas prices fueled by the ongoing conflict with Iran have driven widespread American disapproval of that war. Expanding US military involvement in the region risks further stoking voters' resentment. Houthis say Saudis launch new attacks Yemen's Houthi-run health ministry said Monday that airstrikes on a government complex and a house in the northern province of al-Jawf killed nine people, including five children and a woman, and wounded seven others, according to the Houthi-controlled SABA news agency. Houthi officials also said that Saudi Arabia carried out new strikes on the Yemeni capital of Sanaa, killing one person and wounding 12. The Riyadh airport remained closed on Monday, and workers in the capital's financial district were told to work from home. Yet, the Saudis on Monday continued with the second day of the World Petroleum Energy Congress. UAE diplomat suggests Gulf allies respond to Houthis jointly Separately, an Emirati diplomat on Monday called for “joint Gulf action” to defend Gulf countries against attacks by Iran and its allied groups. Anwar Gargash, a diplomatic adviser to the rulers of the United Arab Emirates, said Iran and its allies wrongly assessed that Gulf Arabs were “the weakest link” in the US war against Iran, during which Tehran and its allies repeatedly attacked Arab countries on the other side of the Gulf. “It has become clear that we are all targeted, and that our security is indivisible,” he wrote on social media. Iran's Foreign Ministry on Monday expressed concern about fighting between the Saudis and Houthis and said Iran would be ready to settle disputes. “We are severely concerned about developments in the Arabian Peninsula,” spokesman Esmail Baghaei said at his weekly briefing. “We have many times announced readiness for applying our good offices in order to facilitate talks between the two sides.” Baghaei said Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al-Saud, spoke by phone on Sunday about the situation but did not offer details. Funeral held for Jordanian killed in airport attack Dozens of mourners attended the Monday funeral for a Jordanian killed in the missile strike on King Khalid International Airport. Mahmoud Al-Barqawi, 33, who worked in a Riyadh cafe and was the father of two children, was buried after a funeral procession began at a mosque in Amman. His father, Hasan al-Barqawi, said the family was struggling to cope. “No one can truly feel the pain of this tragedy,” he said. The strike also wounded four Jordanian citizens. Jordan's Royal Court chief Yousef Al-Issawi attended the funeral, offering condolences on behalf of the king and crown prince.

stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13 : The Supreme Court on Tuesday took serious note of allegations that women journalists covering protests in the national capital were assaulted by police personnel and directed a senior Delhi Police officer to remain present during the hearing on Thursday to explain the matter. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana made the observation after senior advocate Indira Jaising mentioned a petition filed by the Network of Women in Media, India (NWMI), seeking safeguards for journalists covering protests, particularly women journalists. "We would like some senior officer to remain present here and explain," the CJI Kant-led Bench said, indicating that the police would have to explain the allegations. The development comes amid allegations that journalists covering protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar were manhandled, detained and obstructed while discharging their professional duties on October 10 and 11. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan also mentioned a separate contempt petition alleging that the police had assaulted journalists in violation of the Supreme Court’s October 10 order. The apex court had directed the authorities to ensure that lawyers, journalists and other professionals were not hindered in discharging their professional duties. The directions were passed by a Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana while hearing contempt petitions alleging violations of its order concerning restrictions imposed ahead of the proposed protest. It had also directed the authorities to ensure the normal functioning of Metro and railway services, uninterrupted internet connectivity and free movement of people, subject to traffic regulations and public order requirements. The Supreme Court had also directed that there should be no detention except in accordance with the procedure established by law, particularly in the case of peaceful and unarmed gatherings outside areas where prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force. --IANS

stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13 : The Reserve Bank of India is likely to stay on tightening path through H1FY28 and may hike the repo rate by around 75 basis points, according to leading brokerages. According to the NDTV Profit report, global brokerages -- including BofA, Goldman Sachs and UBS -- said that the Middle East tensions, energy supply disruptions and intensifying El Nino could push headline CPI higher. BofA and UBS have forecast that the central bank will tighten monetary policy and expect around a 75-basis-point repo rate hike in MPC meetings scheduled for FY27, extending up to the first half of fiscal 2028. Apart from that, UBS predicted full-year headline inflation to average near 5.2 per cent in FY27, while it could cross 5 per cent through first half of FY28 due to adverse weather-related strains. "As per our global strategy team, historical evidence suggests that effects typically materialize with a lag of 6-18 months following peak weather disruption. With likely peak occurring between November and February, most significant impact on global food prices may emerge during 2027 and early 2028, adding upside risks to inflation outlook," the brokerage forecasted. Additionally, they flagged upside risks after India's consumer inflation touched a 23-month high in September on surge in food prices. The report highlighted that headline Consumer Price Index inflation came at 5.54 per cent in September, up from 4.8 per cent in August, driven largely by higher food and vegetable prices. Moreover, food inflation climbed to 7.74 per cent in September from 5.97 per cent in August, while food and beverages inflation rose to 7.36 per cent from 5.66 per cent. Notably, rise in inflation was more pronounced in rural areas, where consumer inflation stood at 6.08 per cent in September, compared with 4.88 per cent in urban areas. CPI (General) index for combined category increased to 109.49 in September from 108.74 in August. Similarly, combined CFPI index rose to 112.17 from 110.73 during same period. --IANS

stories.headline: US Democrats’ House victory could test Trump’s India policy
stories.title: US Democrats’ House victory could test Trump’s India policy
stories.summary: Washington, Oct 13 : Democrats are heavy favourites to win control of the US House of Representatives in the November 3 midterm elections, according to the prediction markets and polling averages, raising the prospect of tougher congressional scrutiny of President Donald Trump's tariff, trade and visa policies that weigh heavily on India. Traders on the prediction market Kalshi gave Democrats a 90 per cent chance of taking the House and a 62 per cent chance of winning the Senate, according to prices published on Monday. Kalshi put the chance of a Democratic sweep of both chambers at 61 per cent. The next most likely outcome, at 30 per cent, was a divided Congress with Democrats running the House and Republicans keeping the Senate. The Silver Bulletin polling average, updated on Monday, had Democrats ahead by 8.8 points on the generic congressional ballot, which asks voters which party they will support for Congress. "Democrats' surge in the polls that started in early September still hasn't stopped," the Silver Bulletin said. Trump's own numbers offer his party little cover. A CBS News/YouGov poll conducted from September 30 to October 2 found 39 per cent of Americans approved of his job performance and 61 per cent disapproved. On inflation, only 29 per cent approved and 71 per cent disapproved. The Senate is far less certain. The Cook Political Report rates seven races as toss-ups: Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas. Six of those seats are held by Republicans. A Democratic House would give the party subpoena power and committee gavels. House Democrats are preparing "a vast oversight agenda" covering Trump, his family and his administration, US media said. London-based think tank Chatham House said Democrats' real leverage would be on money, even if they took only the House. The US debt limit is expected to be reached by mid-2027, and a Democratic House alone would rule out Republicans using the budget reconciliation process to raise it, Max Yoeli, a senior research fellow at Chatham House, wrote last month. Yoeli also cautioned that opposition on foreign policy "will be more about optics than hard constraints", since Democrats would lack the votes to override presidential vetoes. For India, that points to a Democratic House making its mark mostly through oversight rather than new law. Trump's tariffs have largely been imposed through executive action. A Democratic House could hold hearings and force votes on them, but would struggle to overturn them against a veto. The same applies to the Graham Act tariffs on top buyers of Russian energy, which could take effect from October 18. The law requires the administration to send Congress a written justification at least 10 days before imposing such duties, a requirement that a Democratic-led House would be well placed to press. Any India-US trade agreement that needs legislation would also face a more sceptical chamber. The $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions, which falls heavily on Indian professionals, is already tied up in court. stories.summary: Mumbai, Oct 13 : BJP leader and former MP Kirit Somaiya has approached the Union Ministry of Home Affairs and immigration authorities, urging them to issue a Look Out Circular (LOC) against actor Imran Khan. He has also requested that the actor be barred from leaving the country until an inquiry into his complaint and the investigation into a Mumbai police case are completed. In a letter dated October 13 to Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Somaiya called on the Ministry of Home Affairs to issue directions preventing Khan from travelling abroad under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. He also asked the Bureau of Immigration to issue an LOC against the actor and notify the police should he attempt to leave India. The move comes after a protest at Mumbai’s August Kranti Maidan on October 10 where demonstrators demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In his letter, Somaiya claimed that the gathering had taken place without the necessary permission. He further alleged that Khan had attended and participated in the protest before Mumbai Police detained him at the venue. According to the letter, Gamdevi Police Station registered an FIR, numbered 813 of 2026, in connection with the incident, with Khan named in the case. Somaiya also stated that he had not received a copy of the FIR. Somaiya claimed in his letter that Khan is a US citizen and reportedly holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card. He urged the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Bureau of Immigration to assess whether the actor’s participation in the protest calls for action under Section 7D of the Citizenship Act, 1955, and the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. He has also sought a written update from the concerned authorities on the steps taken in response to his request. Bengaluru: The Karnataka High Court has struck down the state’s decision to increase reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes beyond the 50% ceiling, ruling the enhanced quota unconstitutional.

stories.headline: Delhi to host first-ever BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ meeting today
stories.title: Delhi to host first-ever BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ meeting today
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13 : India is set to host the first-ever BIMSTEC Home Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi on Tuesday, marking a significant step towards strengthening regional cooperation on security-related issues. Union Home Minister Amit Shah will chair the meeting. Describing the gathering as a historic occasion, HM Shah on Monday said the meeting underscores "our shared resolve to combat terrorism, transnational organised crime, narcotics radicalisation, trafficking, illicit financial flows, and cyber threats". "Through decisive coordination, we remain committed to building a safer, stronger, and more secure BIMSTEC," the Home Minister said. Officials from the member countries are expected to participate in the meeting. The meeting is expected to provide a platform for BIMSTEC member nations to discuss common security concerns and explore ways to enhance cooperation in addressing threats that extend across national borders. The gathering also highlights the importance of coordinated regional efforts to counter terrorism, organised criminal networks, drug-related threats, human trafficking and cybercrime. BIMSTEC, an acronym for the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation, is a regional organisation comprising seven member countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. According to the organisation's official website, BIMSTEC works to strengthen collaboration in areas such as agriculture and food security, the blue economy, connectivity, culture, disaster management, energy, environment and climate change, fiscal and monetary policy, health, human resource development, fisheries and livestock, and people-to-people relations, among other fields. In July this year, the 5th Meeting of the BIMSTEC National Security Chiefs was held in New Delhi, where the National Security Advisers and heads of delegations exchanged views on various measures to combat terrorism and organised crime; ensure security in the cyber, maritime and energy domains; enhance connectivity; facilitate efficient disaster management; and tackle new and emerging security threats. The meeting adopted the BIMSTEC Guidelines for the Maritime Component of Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief. The guidelines will help BIMSTEC member states undertake relief operations in the region in an expeditious manner. They also endorsed a set of Guiding Principles on the Conduct of Maritime Law Enforcement Agencies during Interactions at Sea. These principles are expected to provide reference points for increasing predictability and promoting safety during maritime engagements among member states. --IANS

article_sentences: The South Peninsula is bracing for the arrival of the north-east monsoon, with the seasonal reversal of winds expected to gather momentum alongside the retreat of the south-west monsoon.

The trigger could be a low-pressure area forecast to develop over the south-east Bay of Bengal anytime now, setting the stage for the easterly flows that herald the onset of the second rainy season for the water-starved region.
The atmospheric signals are falling into place, with an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the South Andaman Sea poised to descend to lower levels and consolidate into the crucial low-pressure area.
At the western end of the Bay, another cyclonic circulation over the Gulf of Mannar could help draw in and channel the easterly winds, carrying the north-east monsoon deeper into the South Peninsula.
With the Bay of Bengal primed for a fresh low-pressure system and the retreating monsoon nearing its final exit, the South Peninsula is entering a consequential phase of the seasonal calendar.

The coming days will determine how quickly the easterlies take charge, and whether the expected onset of north-east monsoon brings a sustained spell of rain to the region after the south-west monsoon’s long retreat.
The emerging weather pattern is already offering a foretaste of the transition, with rain, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds unfolding over several parts of southern India.
These conditions could intensify on either side of October 15, around which the north-east monsoon is likely to set in over Tamil Nadu and adjoining areas.
Its formal arrival could be announced during this phase.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD), in its Tuesday morning assessment, said conditions were becoming favourable for the south-west monsoon to withdraw from the remaining parts of the country and for north-east monsoon rains to commence over the South Peninsula simultaneously during the next 2-3 days.
The withdrawal line of the four-month south-west monsoon, which officially ended on September 30, continues to pass through Kolkata, Angul, Khammam and Honavar.
The predecessor monsoon must complete its retreat from the mainland before the seasonal transition is fully established, although the two processes can overlap in time.
